evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister to arrest a downward economic spiral and restart IMF talks.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new finance minister faces tight time frame to tackle crises
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister to arrest a downward economic spiral and restart IMF talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous reporting syndicated by Euronews, with direct description of the appointment and task.
evidence.period_fit: April 2022 accession and early stabilization period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sharif's cabinet choice; later constrained by inherited crisis conditions.
contrary_evidence: The appointment occurred inside a severe economic and coalition crisis.
It did not prevent later cabinet turnover.

evidence.claim: PML-N stalwart Ishaq Dar was nominated by Nawaz Sharif and PM Shehbaz and appointed finance minister after Miftah Ismail resigned, amid internal disagreement over fuel-price decisions.
evidence.title: Ishaq Dar appointed federal finance and revenue minister
evidence.excerpt: PML-N stalwart Ishaq Dar was nominated by Nawaz Sharif and PM Shehbaz and appointed finance minister after Miftah Ismail resigned, amid internal disagreement over fuel-price decisions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with the Cabinet Division notification and named attribution to the PM's advice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's advice and the party leadership's preferences.
contrary_evidence: Dar is a political stalwart rather than a neutral technocrat.
The replacement suggests loyalty politics alongside expertise.

evidence.claim: The government said it would raise taxes on the rich and ban government officials from buying new cars in the 2022/23 budget to reduce the deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.title: Pakistan to raise taxes on rich, ban some car buying to secure IMF bailout
evidence.excerpt: The government said it would raise taxes on the rich and ban government officials from buying new cars in the 2022/23 budget to reduce the deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on an official budget announcement and the policy content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct cabinet policy under Sharif, though prepared through the finance ministry.
contrary_evidence: Mostly a stabilization and austerity measure rather than a growth program.
Immediate burdens rose during a crisis year.

evidence.claim: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said the government ended fuel subsidies and raised prices to trim the fiscal deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.title: Pakistan further removes fuel subsidies to win IMF funding
evidence.excerpt: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said the government ended fuel subsidies and raised prices to trim the fiscal deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous report on a directly announced policy shift.
evidence.period_fit: June 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct policy choice under Sharif; it also unwound an inherited subsidy package.
contrary_evidence: The move was inflationary and politically costly.
It mainly reversed a predecessor policy rather than creating new prosperity.

evidence.claim: The State Bank raised the policy rate to 15 percent to control spiraling inflation after a 13-year-high inflation reading.
evidence.title: SBP raises policy rate by 125bps to 15pc
evidence.excerpt: The State Bank raised the policy rate to 15 percent to control spiraling inflation after a 13-year-high inflation reading.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous central-bank reporting in a major Pakistani outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: SBP is independent, but the move reflects the macro regime under Sharif's government.
contrary_evidence: Rate hikes show stabilization effort, but also the severity of the macro crisis.
Monetary tightening alone could not offset fiscal and external stress.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Pakistani authorities would establish an electronic asset declaration system and review anticorruption institutions, including NAB, to improve governance.
evidence.title: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on the Combined Seventh and Eight Reviews for Pakistan’s Extended Fund Facility
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Pakistani authorities would establish an electronic asset declaration system and review anticorruption institutions, including NAB, to improve governance.
evidence.source_locator: governance and corruption section near the end of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF statement describing government commitments and reform steps.
evidence.period_fit: July 2022, squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif's administration, though implementation depended on institutions and parliament.
contrary_evidence: Commitments are not the same as enacted reform.
The IMF package also reflected crisis pressure and external conditionality.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities had taken important measures and the immediate priorities were FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, expanded social safety, and SOE governance reform.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Completes the Combined Seventh, and Eighth Reviews of the Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities had taken important measures and the immediate priorities were FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, expanded social safety, and SOE governance reform.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official board decision and staff appraisal with specific policy priorities and quantified program context.
evidence.period_fit: Late August 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sharif's government, though much was driven by inherited imbalances and external financing stress.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also said FY22 policy was procyclical and unsustainable.
Corrective action indicates prior mismanagement rather than clean stewardship.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Pakistan already faced double-digit inflation, a sharp rise in imports, rupee pressure, and low investment, exports, and productivity before Sharif’s economic team settled in.
evidence.title: Long-standing Structural Challenges Pose Risks to Pakistan’s Sustained Growth: World Bank Bi-Annual Pakistan Development Update Report
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Pakistan already faced double-digit inflation, a sharp rise in imports, rupee pressure, and low investment, exports, and productivity before Sharif’s economic team settled in.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary multilateral assessment at the start of the period.
evidence.period_fit: April 2022 baseline immediately before and after Sharif took office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited conditions rather than Sharif's own policy record.
contrary_evidence: This is baseline context, not direct evidence of Sharif's choices.
Some pressures predate his government.

evidence.claim: The PDNA estimated damages above USD 14.9 billion, losses about USD 15.2 billion, reconstruction needs of at least USD 16.3 billion, and a poverty increase of 3.7 to 4.0 percentage points affecting 8.4 to 9.1 million more people.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Flood Damages and Economic Losses Over USD 30 billion and Reconstruction Needs Over USD 16 billion - New Assessment
evidence.excerpt: The PDNA estimated damages above USD 14.9 billion, losses about USD 15.2 billion, reconstruction needs of at least USD 16.3 billion, and a poverty increase of 3.7 to 4.0 percentage points affecting 8.4 to 9.1 million more people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint World Bank/Pakistan assessment with quantified losses and poverty impacts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Largely shock-driven and inherited-exposure context rather than pure policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The report is about disaster damage, not direct economic-policy competence.
It limits what can fairly be credited to Sharif.

evidence.claim: Sharif said flood relief assistance under BISP would rise from Rs28 billion to Rs70 billion and each affected family would receive Rs25,000.
evidence.title: PM announces to increase BISP flood relief aid to Rs70b
evidence.excerpt: Sharif said flood relief assistance under BISP would rise from Rs28 billion to Rs70 billion and each affected family would receive Rs25,000.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM announcement carried by the state broadcaster.
contrary_evidence: Emergency cash relief is necessary but temporary.
It does not prove durable income recovery or structural reform.

evidence.claim: The Government of Pakistan and the UN jointly launched the 2022 Floods Response Plan, and the UN said the government had released national funds including immediate cash relief.
evidence.title: Media Update: United Nations Pakistan, 30 August 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Government of Pakistan and the UN jointly launched the 2022 Floods Response Plan, and the UN said the government had released national funds including immediate cash relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN country-office press release summarizing the joint response and cash relief.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif's government but mediated through disaster-response machinery and international partners.
contrary_evidence: This is humanitarian response rather than long-run prosperity.
Much of the spending was forced by disaster rather than discretionary reform.

evidence.claim: UN Women distributed relief items and cash grants to vulnerable women and planned women’s centres and GBV-response services for flood-affected areas.
evidence.title: UN Women puts women and girls at the heart of flood response in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: UN Women distributed relief items and cash grants to vulnerable women and planned women’s centres and GBV-response services for flood-affected areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN reporting with specific interventions for vulnerable groups and women.
evidence.period_fit: September 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to the government’s disaster-response environment rather than uniquely to Sharif.
contrary_evidence: This is relief rather than long-run prosperity.
It shows crisis mitigation more than structural reform.
